question: Group of neurons that are inactive normally is activated in medulla by increased breathing during exercise:
explanation: Medullary respiratory center located in reticular formation Dorsal respiratory group: It is primarily responsible for inspirationand generates the basic rhythm for breathing Input to the dorsal respiratory group comes from the vagus and glossopharyngeal nerves. The vagus nerve relays information from peripheral chemoreceptors and mechanoreceptors in the lung. The glossopharyngeal nerve relays information from peripheral chemoreceptors Output from the dorsal respiratory group travels, via the phrenic nerve, to the diaphragm. Ventral respiratory group It is primarily responsible for expiration and not active during normal, quiet breathing, when expiration is passive. It is activated for example during exercise, when expiration becomes an active process Apneustic center: is located in the lower pons. It stimulates inspiration, producing a deep and prolonged inspiratory gasp (apneusis) Pneumotaxic center: It is located in the upper pons. It inhibits inspiration and, therefore, regulates inspiratory volume and respiratory rate.

The structures traditionally thought of as lying in the transpyloric plane include: Pylorus of the stomach D1 part of the duodenum Duodeno-jejunal flexure Root of the transverse mesocolon Hepatic flexure of the colon Splenic flexure of the colon Fundus of the gallbladder Neck of the pancreas Hila of the kidneys Hilum of the spleen 9th costal cartilage Termination of spinal cord and superior portion of conus medullaris Origin of SMA Splenic vein joins superior mesenteric vein to form portal vein Cisterna chyli
